newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says U.S. troops could guard Hebron settlers.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says U.S. troops could guard Hebron settlers.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Tuesday he was ready to have U.S. troops guard Jewish settlers in the West Bank town of Hebron if that would calm Israeli security fears.

"They (Israel) are repeating security, security. I told them, okay, if you don't trust the joint mobile units and you don't trust your soldiers or our soldiers, okay, why not to call upon the international presence with the participation of the American army," Arafat told a news conference with Jordan's King Hussein in Palestinian-ruled Jericho in the West Bank.
Arafat said American peacekeepers had been stationed in the Egyptian Sinai and elsewhere -- so there was a precedent.
Israeli negotiating team spokesman Moshe Fogel declined comment when asked about such a proposal earlier, saying: "We do not want to go into the details of the various proposals."

Israel and the PLO have been struggling to reach agreement on the long-promised pullback from Israeli-occupied Hebron, the last of seven West Bank cities due to be handed over to Palestinian self-rule under a 1995 peace deal.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, elected in May, has held up the handover while insisting on additional security measures to protect the 400 Jewish settlers in fortified enclaves among 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron.
Palestinians refuse to amend the Hebron accord they signed with the former government, ousted by Netanyahu.

"We said we can ask for American forces to protect the settlers but we will not accept changing the agreement or Israeli intervention in areas under Palestinian jurisdiction," said Nabil Abu Rdainah, an aide to Arafat.
PLO officials had said they rejected an Israeli proposal to station Israeli troops on ridges overlooking Hebron but would agree to deploying joint mobile patrols on them.
According to the Hebron deal signed a year ago, the PLO would have immediate sole responsibility for the ridges but joint patrols could come later "in parts of Hebron".
PLO officials said that in meetings with the Israelis last week they supported not only increasing the number of international observers due to be deployed in Hebron but also arming them.

An Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron should have been carried out in March but was delayed by Israel's previous centre-left government after Islamic suicide bombers killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.
Intensive Israeli-PLO negotiations emerged from an emergency Washington summit called following fierce clashes last month in which 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed.
